sentences.text:
Dheeravath Kumar vs The State Of Telangana on 17 November,
2023
 Hon'Ble Sri Justice J. Sreenivas Rao
 Writ Petition No.31816 of 2023
Order:

entities.text: Dheeravath Kumar vs The State Of Telangana
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: This writ petition is filed to declare the seizure of the petitioner's vehicle i.e., Lorry bearing No. TS 30 TA 4217 under cover of panchanama dated 17.08.2023 in connection with Crime No.561 of 2023 of Medchal Police Station, Cyberabad, as arbitrary and unconstitutional.

2. Heard learned counsel for the petitioner and learned Assistant Government Pleader for Civil Supplies appearing on behalf of respondent Nos.1 to 3.
3.

The vehicle of the petitioner i.e., lorry bearing No. TS 30 TA 4217 was seized under cover of panchanama by respondent No.4 in connection with Crime No.561 of 2023 of Medchal Police Station, Cyberabad.

It is stated that on 17.08.2023, while patrolling the de facto complainant received a credible information that some persons are illegally transporting PDS rice illegally towards Toopran side from ORR Shamirpet side, in that regard conducting vehicle checking at ORR exit No.6, Kandlakoya, Medchal, office of respondent No.4 stopped the vehicle, checked the lorry and found it as PDS rice.
On questioning the driver of the vehicle, he did not produce valid documents pertaining to PDS rice transportation.

On enquiry, it was revealed that his name is Deeravath Kumar, s/o Raveender, driver of the vehicle and owner of the lorry and he was transported the PDS rice illegally and the Inspector of Police, Medchal Police Station, registered a case in Cr.No.561 of 2023, under Section 420 IPC and Section 7 of the Essential Commodities Act,
1955 (for short 'the E.C.Act').
4.
Learned Assistant Government Pleader for Civil Supplies submitted that proceedings under Section 6-A of the E.C.Act, have been initiated against the petitioner and the same are pending.
Learned Assistant Government Pleader further submitted that the subject vehicle is still in the custody of respondent No.4 - Police Station.

5. In view of the above facts and circumstances, taking into consideration the fact that the respondent authorities have initiated proceedings under Section 6-A of the E.C. Act and the same are pending, this Court is inclined to grant relief to the petitioner.

6. Accordingly, this writ petition is disposed of directing the respondents to release the vehicle i.e.,
lorry bearing No. TS 30 TA 4217, under cover of panchanama dated 17.08.2023 in connection with Crime No.561 of 2023 of Medchal Police Station, Cyberabad, in favour of the petitioner subject to condition of his furnishing bank guarantee by way of Fixed Deposit for a sum of Rs.25,000/-
(Rupees Twenty Five Thousand only) in favour of the 2nd respondent-Collector (Civil Supplies),
Medchal-Malkajgiri District.

Release of the vehicle shall be subject to outcome of the confiscation Dheeravath Kumar vs The State Of Telangana on 17 November, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/183082549/
1 proceedings under Section 6-A of the EC Act.
